prompt: Rotate a square matrix 90 degrees clockwise IN PLACE -- same array object, same row objects -- and then handle any number of quarter turns including negative ones. Complete rotateClockwise and rotateTimes in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: A clockwise quarter turn is a transpose followed by reversing every row, and both of those can be done with swaps inside the original array. The transpose only swaps cells above the diagonal (start the inner loop at c = r + 1), because swapping the whole square would undo itself. For rotateTimes the trap is Java's % operator, which returns a negative remainder for a negative left operand, so ((n % 4) + 4) % 4 is needed to fold any int -- positive or negative -- into 0..3.
hints: Two passes are enough: first transpose the matrix (swap matrix[r][c] with matrix[c][r]), then reverse each row left-to-right with a two-pointer swap.
In the transpose loop start the inner index at r + 1. Starting at 0 visits every pair twice and leaves the matrix exactly as it was.
For rotateTimes, -1 % 4 is -1 in Java, not 3. Normalise with ((quarterTurns % 4) + 4) % 4 and then call rotateClockwise that many times.
